skill.name: accessibility-compliance-accessibility-audit
skill.description: Audit web and mobile experiences for WCAG compliance, accessibility barriers, assistive technology compatibility, and practical remediation priorities.
skill.summary: Plan and report accessibility audits using automated checks, manual testing, WCAG mapping, and remediation guidance.

content.value_statement: Accessibility barriers can exclude users and create compliance risk. This skill structures WCAG audits, testing evidence, prioritized findings, and remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Defines audit scope by platform, WCAG level, target pages, and key user journeys.
Provides axe-core, Puppeteer, and jest-axe examples for automated accessibility testing.
Guides manual checks for keyboard access, screen readers, focus order, contrast, reflow, and cognitive accessibility.
Maps barriers to WCAG criteria, severity, user impact, and remediation priorities.
Supplies accessible markup patterns and remediation examples for forms, dialogs, tabs, buttons, and live regions.
Outlines CI testing, artifact reporting, retesting, and ongoing accessibility practices.
limitations: The skill cannot inspect a product without access to its interface, source, design artifacts, or test results.
Automated scans cannot replace manual keyboard, screen reader, zoom, reflow, and user testing.
Recommendations require environment-specific validation and do not constitute legal certification.
Tooling examples may require dependency, runtime, selector, and workflow updates for the target project.

use_cases.title: Review a feature before release
use_cases.description: Assess a new interface against WCAG, rank barriers by impact, and give developers testable remediation steps.

use_cases.title: Run a structured accessibility audit
use_cases.description: Combine automated scans with keyboard, screen reader, focus, contrast, reflow, and content checks.

use_cases.title: Build compliance evidence
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized report with WCAG mappings, testing coverage, ownership, retest status, and remaining limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WCAG AA accessibility checklist for [page or component]. Cover keyboard access, labels, headings, images, focus, contrast, and errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an initial review of one interface.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a user journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [user journey] on [platform] against WCAG [version and level]. Rank barriers by impact and provide clear remediation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing a complete task across several screens.

prompt_templates.title: Plan automated and manual testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an accessibility test plan for [product]. Combine axe-core coverage with keyboard, screen reader, zoom, reflow, contrast, and cognitive checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a team needs repeatable test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Design an accessibility program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an accessibility program for [product] across [platforms]. Include WCAG mapping, CI gates, manual testing, ownership, evidence, remediation tracking, and retesting.

output_examples.input: Audit the checkout form for WCAG AA and prioritize the findings.
output: Critical: Payment errors are shown visually but are not announced to screen readers.
Serious: Several fields have placeholder text without persistent labels.
Moderate: Focus indicators have insufficient contrast on secondary actions.
Next steps: Add an alert summary, associate errors with fields, provide labels, and retest keyboard and screen reader flows.

output_examples.input: Create an accessibility test plan for a responsive navigation menu.
output: Automated coverage: Scan closed and expanded states at desktop and mobile widths.
Keyboard coverage: Verify logical focus order, Enter and Space activation, Escape closure, and focus return.
Screen reader coverage: Confirm button name, expanded state, menu relationships, and announced updates.
Visual coverage: Test focus visibility, 200 percent zoom, 320-pixel reflow, contrast, and reduced motion.

output_examples.input: Summarize accessibility evidence for a release review.
output: Scope: Registration, authentication, account recovery, and profile management on web.
Evidence: Automated scan results, manual keyboard records, screen reader notes, contrast checks, and resolved issue retests.
Open risk: Two moderate issues remain in account recovery and have assigned owners.
Decision: Release after documented acceptance and schedule the remaining fixes for the next maintenance cycle.

best_practices: Confirm platforms, WCAG target, pages, journeys, assistive technologies, permissions, and success criteria before testing.
Combine automated checks with manual testing and record reproducible evidence for every confirmed barrier.
Prioritize by user impact, provide specific fixes, assign ownership, and retest after implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat an automated score as complete evidence of accessibility or compliance.
Do not add ARIA when native semantic HTML already provides the required role and behavior.
Do not report vague failures without affected elements, user impact, WCAG mapping, remediation, and verification steps.

faq.question: Which accessibility standards does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on WCAG A, AA, and AAA criteria, with examples centered on common WCAG 2.1 AA checks.

faq.question: Can this skill certify legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. It provides technical audit guidance and evidence, but legal conclusions require qualified counsel and jurisdiction-specific review.

faq.question: Does an axe-core scan complete the audit?
faq.answer: No. Automated tools detect only some barriers, so manual keyboard, screen reader, zoom, reflow, and cognitive checks remain necessary.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best audit?
faq.answer: Provide the target platform, WCAG level, pages, key journeys, source or interface access, supported browsers, and known assistive technology requirements.

faq.question: Can the skill review mobile applications?
faq.answer: Yes, when platform details and usable artifacts are available. The web-focused code examples must be adapted for native mobile testing tools.

faq.question: How should findings be prioritized?
faq.answer: Prioritize barriers by user impact, task criticality, affected users, frequency, WCAG level, remediation effort, and release risk.
